## Why

Check lines reach role briefs in three places. The spec-check and gate briefs list them under the "Implementer-runnable Check commands", "Check commands ork runs" and "Orchestrator-run Check commands" headings (`internal/engine/brief.go:765-805`). The implementer's Done-when list repeats each Check entry as "Run or report blocked: ENTRY" (`internal/engine/brief.go:435`). A Check line with an unquoted `-run A|B` pattern goes into all of these as written. A read-only role that runs it as written is denied, because the permission check scans an unquoted `|` as a second operation ("multiple operations"). The reviewer hit this in ork run ork-20261122-025921-2e6a, item S434, with `DoctorGolden|TestDoctorUpgradeFlagPrintsEveryTool`.

Owner decisions (adj 659, adj 661, 2026-11-27):
- When ork renders a Check line into a brief, it wraps an unquoted `-run` pattern that contains `|` in single quotes (`-run 'A|B'`). The spec's Check lines stay as stored, and so does the `## Slice` JSON.
- The reviewer brief also gets a Check command list, built the way the gate's is, with the quoted form. Today only the gate and spec-check briefs have one (`internal/engine/brief.go:293`).

Both permission matchers already accept the quoted form, and tests cover it today. These are `checkCommandRunnable` (`TestCheckCommandRunnableQuotedPipe`, `internal/engine/brief_test.go:1046`) and the hook's `ApprovalPolicy.Evaluate` (`TestEvaluateQuotedPipeIsNotAnOperator`, `internal/agent/claude/pretool_test.go:252`). One guard test is added for the pinned `go -C DIR test*` form a read-only role actually holds.

Owner decisions, 2026-11-27: adj 659 (quote an unquoted -run pattern with | in single quotes when a Check line is rendered into a brief) and adj 661 (the reviewer brief gets a Check command list built like the gate's).

## Failing tests

- TestQuoteRunPipePattern (`internal/engine/brief_test.go`, new): a table over the helper that quotes the pattern.
  - `go test ./internal/cli -run A|B -v` becomes `go test ./internal/cli -run 'A|B' -v`.
  - `go test ./internal/cli -run=A|B` becomes `go test ./internal/cli -run='A|B'`.
  - The command comes back unchanged when the pattern has no `|`, is already single- or double-quoted, or holds `;`, `&`, `<`, `>`, `$`, a backtick or a backslash.
  - The command comes back unchanged when the `|` starts or ends the word, or is a word of its own, as in `go test ./... | tee out`.
  - `-run A|B && make check` quotes only the pattern, giving `-run 'A|B' && make check`.
- TestGateBriefQuotesARunPatternWithAPipe (`internal/engine/brief_test.go`, new): a gate brief whose Check section is ``- `go test ./internal/cli -run A|B` `` (with `in.Allow = DefaultImplementerAllowlist("")`). Today the line lands under "Orchestrator-run".

## Implement

1. Write the tests above first and confirm the five `internal/engine` tests fail.
2. In `internal/engine/brief.go`, add `quoteRunPipe(command string) string`. It splits the command into words on whitespace outside quotes. A word `-run` is followed by a pattern word, or the word is `-run=PATTERN`. When that pattern contains `|` that is not first, last or doubled, and contains no quote, backslash, `$`, backtick, `;`, `&`, `<`, `>` or newline, it is wrapped in single quotes. Every other word and the whitespace stay byte for byte. Nothing else is rewritten.
3. Add `quoteRunPipeSpans(entry string) string`. It applies `quoteRunPipe` to the backtick spans of a Check entry (odd indexes after `strings.Split(entry, "`")`) and leaves the text outside the backticks alone.
4. In `checkCommandSections`, set `command := quoteRunPipe(entry.command)` and pass it to `checkCommandRunnable` and `checkRunByOrk`. List the quoted command. `sliceCheckCommands` and `checkBodyCommands` stay as they are, so ork's own check rows and `SliceCheckCommandWarnings` still read the stored text.
5. In `doneWhen` (`RoleImplementer` branch), build the "Run or report blocked: " item from `quoteRunPipeSpans(entry)`.
6. In `BuildBrief`, extend the condition at `internal/engine/brief.go:293` to `in.Role == RoleGate || in.Role == RoleReviewer || (in.Role == RoleSpecCheck && !in.Carve)`. Leave the `## Slice` block as it is.
7. In `internal/engine/round.go`, move the `ResolvePermission(e.proj, RoleImplementer)` and `in.Allow = PinGitC(implementerPerm.Allow, rec.Worktree)` lines out of the gate-only branch. They run for the gate and the reviewer, and the rest of the gate branch stays gate-only. The reviewer is read-only, so `in.Allow` only feeds the list and no "Allowed forms" item is printed (`internal/engine/brief.go:379`).
8. In `docs/design.md`, in the check-command split paragraph (`docs/design.md:1948-1969`), say that spec-check, gate and reviewer briefs and the implementer's Done-when items show an unquoted `-run` pattern that contains `|` in single quotes (S526, adj 659 and adj 661). Say the reviewer brief now has the same command lists, that the `## Slice` JSON and the spec's own Check lines stay as stored, and that ork's check rows run the stored text.
9. Run `slicer changelog add S526 --root DIR --text "..."` with one bullet for the change.
10. Run the focused tests, then `go test ./...`, `go vet ./...` and `gofmt -l .`.
